engrave.colour_note: Ponoko recommends blue stroke = cut, red stroke = line engrave, gray fill = area engrave (https://help.ponoko.com/en/articles/2688732-how-should-i-specify-laser-actions, checked 2026-10-10); it lets you assign any function to any colour at upload, so check the assignment. The art is the gray fill; every single-line mark (part letters, joint numbers, faceplate glue-up lines, coupon ticks) is a red stroke.
engrave.dxf_layer_note: ENGRAVE holds the art (fill it); LABELS holds every red mark (line engrave).
engrave.dxf_note: DXF has no fill attribute: the engraved art is closed polylines on layer ENGRAVE, so set that layer to fill / raster in the laser software.
conventions: Cuts are kerf-offset; engraving is not.
Engraving stays at least 0.35 mm from every cut.
Parts with art lie outside face up. Parts flagged 'flipped' are mirrored in the cut + engrave files for this; the art is not mirrored. Never flip a part to engrave a second side.
Parts without art lie inside face up and carry red joint marks: the same number on the two edges that meet.
The drawer faceplate glue-up lines are in the cut + labels files only.

order: Cut the coupon first, on a scrap of your real plywood.
Measure the kerf square (this gives your measured kerf, k) and the thickness slots.
Pick the thickness set, then try the finger pairs: the pairs decide the kerf set.
coupon_guide.orientation: Hold the coupon with the clipped corner at the top left. The thickness slots run from the narrowest (2.5 mm drawn) at the left to the widest (3.4 mm) at the right. In the marked file the ticks sit between the slots and the magnet holes (below the slots as the file is drawn).
coupon_guide.marks: In the marked coupon (and the cut + labels sets) every engraved mark is a red hairline.
coupon_guide.kerf_means: k is always the kerf you MEASURED from the kerf square, never the kerf of a file set.

rules.thickness_set: the estimate rounded to 0.1 mm, half up (3.35 goes to 3.4)
rules.kerf_set: the set whose finger pair goes together with firm hand pressure and no rattle (the tighter one if two do)

features.measure: outside width of the cut square, with calipers; measure it in two directions and average
features.then: k is your measured kerf. The nearest set is your first guess; the finger pairs decide (see finger_joints). Kerf varies along the bed and with the plywood: cut and measure the square where the box will be cut, and average two readings if they differ.

features.reading: the narrowest slot your plywood slides into without force; if it is between two slots (tight in one, loose in the next) take the tighter, narrower one
features.formula: thickness = W + k - 0.05, where W is that slot's drawn width and k is the measured kerf
features.rounding: round to the nearest 0.1 mm thickness set, half up: a result of exactly x.x5 goes to the thicker set
features.ticks: the marked coupon has i engraved ticks between slot i and the magnet holes (1 = the narrowest)
features.range: the cut slots are 2.5 + k ... 3.4 + k mm wide, so every plywood from 2.8 to 3.5 mm shows up at any kerf from 0.10 to 0.22 mm; if it enters the first slot with room to spare, use the 2.8 set

features.formula: cut hole = drawn diameter + k; the box wants a 5.65 mm hole for a 6.0 mm magnet
features.reading: the hole a 6 x 2 mm magnet pushes into with firm finger pressure and stays in
features.then: If the smallest hole is already loose, the box holes will be loose too: add a drop of glue. If even the largest is tight, ream the 4 magnet holes lightly.

features.identify: the pairs differ in size: the smallest pair is the diode set, the middle one CO2, the largest Ponoko; the marked coupon also has 1, 2 or 3 engraved ticks on both pieces
features.same_as_the_box: the pairs have the same finger width, play (0.1 mm) and kerf compensation as the box joints: a pair that fits here fits the box
features.reading: press each finger piece into the hole piece of the same size
features.decision: take the pair that goes together with firm hand pressure and no rattle; that is the kerf set to cut. If two pairs do, take the tighter one, as long as it still goes together by hand without a tool. If none goes together by hand take the smallest set and file the fingers.
features.clearance_by_pair: a pair made for kerf s on a laser with measured kerf k has 0.1 + 2 x (k - s) mm of clearance along the fingers

along_the_fingers.what: the fit along the length of the fingers depends on the KERF, not on the thickness
along_the_fingers.tight: the pair will not go together by hand: it was made for a larger kerf than yours: take the next smaller kerf set
along_the_fingers.loose: the fingers rattle sideways in their slots: it was made for a smaller kerf than yours: take the next larger kerf set and test that pair

through_the_thickness.what: the fit through the plywood thickness depends on the THICKNESS, not on the kerf
through_the_thickness.tight: the plywood will not slide through the slot and the fingers end below the surface: your plywood is thicker than the set: use the next thicker thickness set
through_the_thickness.loose: the plywood rattles through the slot and the fingers stand proud of the surface: your plywood is thinner: use the next thinner thickness set

features.reading: slide the lid strip into the slot block (cut for this set's kerf)
features.right: slides freely with a little vertical play (about 1.2 mm total)
